text_blocks.snippet: Female genital eczema, also known as vulvar eczema or vulvar dermatitis, can manifest as itchy, red, swollen, and/or thickened patches of skin on the vulva, the external female genitalia. These patches may also appear darker than the surrounding skin, and some individuals may experience a wet or raw sensation due to damaged skin. The affected skin can also be dry, scaly, and/or cracked.
snippet_highlighted_words: itchy, red, swollen, and/or thickened patches of skin on the vulva, the external female genitalia

list.title: Appearance:
list.snippet: The vulva may have patches of skin that are red, swollen, or darker than the surrounding skin. These patches can be dry, scaly, or thickened. Some people may also experience a wet or raw feeling due to damaged skin.

list.title: Symptoms:
list.snippet: The primary symptom is itching, which can be intense and lead to scratching. Other symptoms may include burning, stinging, or pain, particularly during intercourse or when inserting a tampon or speculum.

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: Vulvar eczema can affect the labia (the folds of skin surrounding the vaginal opening), the perineum (the area between the vaginal opening and the anus), and the skin between the buttocks.

list.title: Flaking and Cracking:
list.snippet: In some cases, the affected skin can be dry, scaly, and crack, leading to potential bleeding.

list.title: Secondary Infections:
list.snippet: Due to the damaged skin, secondary infections with bacteria or yeast can occur, causing further inflammation and discharge.

list.title: Impact:
list.snippet: Vulvar eczema can significantly impact a person's quality of life due to the discomfort, itching, and potential pain it can cause.

list.snippet: Yeast Infections (Candidiasis): Often cause a red, itchy rash with a thick, white, cottage cheese-like discharge.
Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs): STIs like herpes, syphilis, and human papillomavirus (HPV) can cause sores, bumps, or rashes.
Bacterial Infections: Can cause inflammation and irritation.
Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis): Can cause dryness, redness, and itching, and may affect the groin area.
Psoriasis: Can cause red, raised patches with silvery scales, and may occur in the genital area.
Contact Dermatitis: An allergic reaction or irritation from substances like soaps, detergents, or lotions can cause a rash.
Jock Itch: Fungal infection causing a red, itchy rash in the groin area.
Scabies: Caused by mites that burrow into the skin, causing intense itching.
Pubic Lice: Parasitic insects that live in pubic hair.
Irritation from Sweating or Tight Clothing: Can lead to chafing and rashes.
Razor Burn: Can occur after shaving the pubic area.
